lessons.title: Fret lightly, release cleanly
lessons.goal: Sound a fretted note with the minimum useful pressure.
steps: Support the guitar on a stable leg or strap; keep the wrist near neutral and thumb behind the neck without clamping.
Play first-string F4 at fret 1 just behind the fret wire, then reduce pressure until it buzzes and add only enough to clear it.
Alternate open E and fretted F; release finger pressure between notes while keeping the fingertip near the string.
lessons.pattern: String 1: 0-1-0-1; four quarter notes
quiz: A clear fretted note usually needs...
A fingertip just behind the wire and modest pressure
A finger centred on the metal wire

lessons.title: Read your first tab
lessons.goal: Translate string and fret numbers into pitches.
steps: The top tab line is thin string 1, high E; the bottom is thick string 6, low E.
On string 1, read 0-1-3-1 as E-F-G-F; 0 means open, not silent.
Count one quarter-note beat per number, then write a two-bar tab and label the string so octave choices stay clear.
lessons.pattern: e|0-1-3-1|; each number one quarter beat

lessons.title: Hear one fret and two
lessons.goal: Distinguish a semitone from a whole tone.
steps: Play first-string E-F using frets 0-1 and sing the small distance.
Play E-F# with 0-2 and compare the wider whole tone.
Ask a helper to alternate the pairs unseen, then verify by counting frets; listen before looking at the finger.
lessons.pattern: String 1: 0-1 (semitone); 0-2 (whole tone)
quiz: Two frets on the same string span...

lessons.title: Pick and leave silence
lessons.goal: Count through a quarter-note rest without letting the string ring.
steps: At 40 BPM pick open E on 1, 2 and 4; silence beat 3 with a gentle picking-hand touch.
Count the rest aloud even though no note sounds.
Repeat on B3 then G3. Make the muting movement as relaxed as the attack rather than stopping your entire arm.
lessons.pattern: | E E rest E | B B rest B | G G rest G |; quarter beats
quiz: To produce the written rest you must...
Stop the ringing while keeping the count

lessons.title: Original piece: String Lantern
lessons.goal: Play two tab bars with an intentional held ending.
steps: On string 1 play frets 0-1-3-1 as quarters.
Second bar: fret 0 held for two beats, then two silent beats.
Join the bars twice, returning the picking hand to a comfortable position after each attack; use the ladder only after clean releases.

units.title: A small map of the neck

lessons.title: Down and up without tension
lessons.goal: Alternate picking directions on one string.
steps: Hold a pick so only a small tip protrudes; or use relaxed alternating fingers if you play fingerstyle.
On open B3 alternate down-up for eight slow eighth notes; use a small wrist motion.
Add string-2 fret 1 C4 and fret 3 D4, one attack per subdivision. Stop and reset if the hand grips.
lessons.pattern: B string: 0-1-3-1 repeated; eighths, down-up alternation
quiz: A rigid elbow for every note

lessons.title: C major across two strings
lessons.goal: Play C-D-E-F-G with a consistent fingering plan.
steps: Use string 2 frets 1,3 for C4,D4 and string 1 frets 0,1,3 for E4,F4,G4.
Use fretting fingers 1 and 3 at frets 1 and 3; allow the open string to connect positions.
Ascend and descend slowly, saying names; mute the previous string if it should not overlap.
lessons.pattern: B:1,3; e:0,1,3; reverse; one quarter per note

lessons.title: Tab needs durations too
lessons.goal: Read pitch locations and written durations independently.
steps: Play B-string 1-3 then e-string 0, with durations one, one and two beats.
Tab numbers locate notes; use stems in a score or the written counts here to know duration.
Write a second bar e:3(1),1(1),0(2). Clap both bars before adding the finger changes.
quiz: Tab fret numbers alone tell you...
Pitch location, not a complete rhythm

lessons.title: Thirds and fifths on the neck
lessons.goal: Hear C-E and C-G as a third and fifth.
steps: Play C4 on B-string fret 1, then E4 open string 1; sing the major third.
Play C4 then G4 string 1 fret 3; count the letter names C-D-E-F-G to see the fifth.
Play both strings together only when fretted C stays clear. These pairs are chord tones, not full strummed triads.
lessons.pattern: C-E; C-G; compare interval pairs

lessons.title: Original piece: Little Path
lessons.goal: Perform a two-string melody with even note lengths.
steps: Play | C D E G | F E D C | using the two-string locations from the scale fragment.
Keep the pick or fingers close to each string so crossing does not add a pause.
Repeat softly, sing the melody, and try an original two-bar answer ending C; write all four beats.
lessons.pattern: | B:1 B:3 e:0 e:3 | e:1 e:0 B:3 B:1 |; quarters

lessons.title: Check a chord string by string
lessons.goal: Remove accidental muted notes from E minor.
steps: Em low-to-high shape is 0-2-2-0-0-0. Pick each string slowly rather than strumming to hide buzzes.
Arch fretting fingers only enough to avoid touching adjacent strings; keep shoulders relaxed.
Strum once for four beats, release pressure and rest four. Recheck any muted string instead of tightening the whole hand.
lessons.pattern: Em 022000; six separate tones then a four-beat chord
quiz: A muted adjacent string is often helped by...

lessons.title: E minor's three-note family
lessons.goal: Name E, G and B in an E-minor chord.
steps: Find E2 open string 6, G3 open string 3 and B3 open string 2.
Sing E-G, a minor third, then E-B, a fifth; notice chord shapes repeat some note names.
Pick Em tones from low to high and label each E, G or B; six strings do not mean six different chord tones.
lessons.pattern: E G B; Em contains only those pitch classes

lessons.title: Eighths with a measured mute
lessons.goal: Stop a chord on a written rest while the arm keeps time.
steps: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & while the strumming motion continues gently.
Sound Em on 1,2 and 3, then mute on 4; silent upstrokes still track the subdivisions.
Repeat at 40 BPM. A rest is not a slap unless a percussive sound is explicitly intended.
lessons.pattern: Em downstrums on 1,2,3; rest beat 4; silent upstroke motion
quiz: During silent strums the arm can...

lessons.title: Open E minor pentatonic
lessons.goal: Play E-G-A-B-D-E in first position.
steps: Use E2 string6 open, G2 string6 fret3, A2 string5 open, B2 string5 fret2, D3 string4 open, E3 string4 fret2.
Use fingers 3 and 2 for those frets, resting the hand between repetitions.
Ascend, sing the five distinct tones, then play a small answer ending E. Do not let unused bass strings drone unintentionally.
lessons.pattern: E:0,3; A:0,2; D:0,2; open E-minor pentatonic

lessons.title: Original piece: First Rock
lessons.goal: Combine a short bass riff with an Em chord.
steps: Bar 1 quarter-note riff E2-G2-A2-B2; bar 2 Em held for four beats.
Mute the riff's low strings before strumming so the chord attack remains clear.
Repeat four cycles, then change the final riff note from B to D as an intentional variation; keep the two-bar structure.
lessons.pattern: | E:0 E:3 A:0 A:2 | Em(4) |; alternate riff and chord

lessons.title: Em-Am with an anchor
lessons.goal: Change chords without losing the fretting-hand plan.
steps: Em is 022000; Am is x02210, skipping low string 6.
Compare shared second-fret movements and place Am's first-fret C without letting the wrist collapse.
Use four beats per chord, moving fingers during the final release rather than stopping the next beat 1. Practise two changes, rest, repeat.
lessons.pattern: | Em(4) | Am(4) |; low E skipped for Am
quiz: Which string is skipped in standard Am?

lessons.title: A minor's first five notes
lessons.goal: Play A-B-C-D-E from open position.
steps: Use A2 open string5, B2 fret2, C3 fret3; D3 open string4 and E3 fret2.
Say the letters and hear the half step B-C.
Sing a five-note phrase ending A, then play it; compare its home with an E-minor ending.
lessons.pattern: A:0,2,3; D:0,2; reverse; quarters
quiz: The half step in A-B-C-D-E is...

lessons.title: Repeat signs and first endings
lessons.goal: Follow a repeated two-bar map.
steps: Write | Em | Am | with a repeat instruction; perform four bars total.
Number the first pass 1-2 and second pass 3-4 so repeats do not create extra pauses.
Then change the second pass's last bar to Em as an alternate ending; say the roadmap before playing.
lessons.pattern: Two-bar Em-Am repeated; optional second ending Em instead of Am

lessons.title: Thumb and two fingers
lessons.goal: Play an even bass-treble picking pattern.
steps: On Am use thumb on string5 A2, index on string3 A3, middle on string2 C4, index on string3 again.
Play p-i-m-i as four quarters without pulling the treble strings away from the guitar.
Keep bass slightly louder only on beat 1; compare one picked bar with one gently strummed Am bar.
lessons.pattern: Am: A:0 G:2 B:1 G:2; p-i-m-i quarters
quiz: The thumb's role in this pattern is...

lessons.title: Original piece: Evening Answer
lessons.goal: Arrange an Em-Am four-bar phrase with two textures.
steps: Bars 1-2 strum Em-Am once per bar for four beats.
Bars 3-4 fingerpick Em then Am as bass-G-B-G, one quarter per note.
Invent a short treble answer E-G-E or A-C-A between cycles; write its durations so the next first beat arrives on time.
lessons.pattern: | Em(4) | Am(4) | Em p-i-m-i | Am p-i-m-i |
quiz: The four-bar form and beat count

lessons.title: Major versus minor D
lessons.goal: Compare D major and D minor chord tones.
steps: D major xx0232 contains D-F#-A; D minor xx0231 replaces F# with F on string1.
Pick strings 4-1 one at a time, skipping strings 6 and 5.
Alternate four beats D then Dm; sing the third's downward semitone and check that open D keeps the same root.
lessons.pattern: D xx0232; Dm xx0231; four beats each

lessons.title: G major in open position
lessons.goal: Play a G-major octave including F#.
steps: Start G2 string6 fret3; A2 string5 open, B2 fret2, C3 fret3; D3 string4 open, E3 fret2, F#3 fret4, G3 string3 open.
Use a small position adjustment for fret4 rather than forcing a painful stretch.
Ascend and descend at 50 BPM, name F#, then write the one-sharp signature beside the pattern.

lessons.title: I-IV-V by letter and degree
lessons.goal: Translate chord degrees in G and C.
steps: In G, I-IV-V means G-C-D; in C it means C-F-G.
Strum G-C-D-G once per four-beat bar while saying the numerals.
Write the same function in C, then try C-F-G-C with the partial F shape; if the hand fatigues, use triad tones separately.
lessons.pattern: G: I-IV-V-I = G-C-D-G; C: C-F-G-C
quiz: The IV chord in G major is...

lessons.title: An added ninth, not a minor third
lessons.goal: Hear the extra D in Cadd9.
steps: Compare C x32010 with Cadd9 x32033, avoiding low E in both.
Name C-E-G-D and notice the third E remains; an added ninth does not replace the third as a suspension would.
Pick chord tones slowly then use Cadd9-G for two bars, listening to common upper G and D tones.
lessons.pattern: Cadd9 x32033 -> G 320003; four beats each

lessons.title: Original piece: Open Window
lessons.goal: Accompany a four-chord phrase with clean open changes.
steps: Use G-D-Em-C, one bar each; strum on beats 1 and 3.
Before the next bar release unnecessary pressure and move as a planned shape, not one late finger at a time.
Sing a melody from G-A-B-D-E over the changes; repeat with Cadd9 in bar4, keeping the root progression intact.
lessons.pattern: | G | D | Em | C |; strums 1,3; optional Cadd9
quiz: The third chord in this form is...

lessons.title: Tie the offbeat over a beat
lessons.goal: Let an upstroke ring across the next numbered beat.
steps: Count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & with continuous down-up motion.
Sound C on 1, the & of 2, and 4; let the & of 2 ring through beat3 while the hand moves silently.
Write attack marks above the count, then practise the pattern over C-G-Am-F. The tie changes attacks, not the number of beats.
lessons.pattern: Attack 1,2&,4; sustain across 3; repeat per chord
quiz: At tied beat 3, the strumming hand should...
Move silently without a new sounding attack

lessons.title: Six-eight rolling strum
lessons.goal: Group six eighths into two broad beats.
steps: Count 1-la-li 2-la-li and lightly accent subdivisions 1 and 4.
On Am play six gentle alternating attacks, then reduce to one bass note and two treble strums per group.
Move Am-Em once per bar. Use the click as the dotted-quarter pulse; the app's four-beat backing is not a 6/8 accompaniment.
lessons.pattern: 6/8 Am: bass-treble-treble, bass-treble-treble
quiz: The principal accents in six subdivisions fall on...

lessons.title: Light palm-muted rock pulse
lessons.goal: Dampen low notes without choking every attack.
steps: Rest the picking-hand edge lightly near the bridge on the bass strings; move away if notes become completely dead.
Play low E eighths, alternating two muted bars and two open bars.
Add E-B dyad at string6 open and string5 fret2; assess damping by listening, since single-pitch detection does not grade dyads.
lessons.pattern: E-B dyad on eighths; two palm-muted bars, two open
quiz: Light contact and position near the bridge

lessons.title: Roots and fifths in rock
lessons.goal: Move E5-G5-A5 dyads without adding a third.
steps: E5 uses E2-B2; G5 uses string6 fret3 G2 and string5 fret5 D3; A5 uses frets5 and7.
The symbol 5 indicates root and fifth, so these dyads are neither major nor minor by themselves.
Use relaxed two-finger shapes, four beats per chord. Mute unused strings with light contact and rest if the reach feels strained.

lessons.title: Original piece: Road Pulse
lessons.goal: Perform a syncopated four-bar rock accompaniment.
steps: Use Em-G-Am-C one bar each with attacks on 1,2&,4.
First clap the pattern and name each chord on beat1, then add muted bass on beat1 if comfortable.
Repeat one soft cycle and one stronger cycle without changing tempo; record weak rhythm when the offbeat drifts.
lessons.pattern: Em-G-Am-C; sounding strums 1,2&,4; four 4/4 bars
quiz: The agreed tempo and offbeat placement

lessons.title: A minor blues passing note
lessons.goal: Add Eb to an A-minor pentatonic phrase.
steps: At fifth position use string6 frets5,8; string5 frets5,6,7 for A-C-D-Eb-E.
Eb links D to E as a passing tone; sing its tension before playing.
Make a four-beat phrase A-C-D-Eb-E, placing Eb briefly between D and E; finish on A or E rather than always resting on Eb.
lessons.pattern: A C D Eb E; E string5,8; A string5,6,7

lessons.title: A7, D7 and E7
lessons.goal: Play three dominant-seventh open chords.
steps: Use A7 x02020, D7 xx0212 and E7 020100; pick each sounded string to check clarity.
Name roots A,D,E and their minor sevenths G,C,D.
Strum four beats per chord with the correct bass string. Compare each seventh chord to its major triad by hearing the added tension.

lessons.title: Twelve bars on paper
lessons.goal: Follow an A blues without losing the turnaround.
steps: Write A7 for bars1-4, D7 for5-6, A7 for7-8, E7 for9, D7 for10, A7 for11, E7 for12.
Play a single strum each bar and count bar numbers aloud; the last E7 leads to the next A7.
Add a simple quarter-note bass pulse only when the form is memorised. Use your own click, not the app's Em-Am backing.
lessons.pattern: 12 bars: A7 A7 A7 A7 D7 D7 A7 A7 E7 D7 A7 E7
quiz: The turnaround chord in bar12 here is...

lessons.title: Long-short shuffle feel
lessons.goal: Play triplet-based long-short pairs without speeding up.
steps: Count 1-trip-let and strike on 1 and let at 50 BPM.
Play A2-E3 pairs with string5 open and string4 fret2; keep the next beat1 aligned.
Alternate straight eighths and shuffle pairs, hearing the difference. This triplet model is a starting point, not a universal swing ratio.
lessons.pattern: Four A-E long-short pairs per bar; first and third triplet subdivisions
quiz: The short note is placed on...

lessons.title: Original piece: Dusty Shoes
lessons.goal: Create a call and response in twelve-bar A blues.
steps: Call with A-C-D-E over the first two A7 bars; leave a beat after each four-note idea by using eighths then space.
Repeat then vary the ending over D7, targeting D or F# to hear its harmony.
Answer in bars9-12 and resolve to A at the restart. Write the rhythm and chord tones; compare minor-pentatonic colour with the major third C# in A7.
lessons.pattern: A-blues call/response; minor pentatonic colour, chord-tone landings
quiz: A strong landing tone over D7 is...

lessons.title: The written guitar octave
lessons.goal: Relate sounding E3 to written E4.
steps: Guitar treble notation conventionally sounds an octave below the written note; the staff guide labels written pitch.
Play sounding E3 at string4 fret2 and match it to written E4 on the bottom treble line.
Compare tab for string1 open E4 with written E5. Keep mic targets in sounding pitch, not the staff's written octave.
lessons.pattern: Sounding E3-G3-B3-E4; written E4-G4-B4-E5

lessons.title: F major near the nut
lessons.goal: Play an F-major octave with Bb.
steps: Use string4 fret3 F3; string3 open G3, fret2 A3, fret3 Bb3; string2 fret1 C4, fret3 D4; string1 open E4, fret1 F4.
Plan one finger per nearby fret and avoid collapsing the wrist on fret1.
Ascend and descend, saying Bb clearly; play a four-note phrase F-A-Bb-C and sing its whole-tone/semitone changes.

lessons.title: Four-finger arpeggio
lessons.goal: Play p-i-m-a with even volume and small movements.
steps: On C use thumb string5 fret3 C3, index string3 open G3, middle string2 fret1 C4, ring string1 open E4.
Play p-i-m-a as four quarters, letting adjacent tones overlap intentionally.
Reverse a-m-i-p gently; keep the ring finger close instead of lifting it high. If tension appears, practise only p-i-m and add a later.
lessons.pattern: C: A3-G0-B1-e0; p-i-m-a then reverse
quiz: The a finger in fingerstyle notation is...

lessons.title: Root and fifth underneath
lessons.goal: Alternate bass notes while upper fingers keep a pattern.
steps: On C play thumb C3 at string5 fret3 on1 and G2 string6 fret3 on3.
Add index string3 on2 and middle string2 on4; rehearse the thumb alone first.
Change to G: bass G2 on1 and D3 string4 open on3. Keep every bass note shorter if overlapping roots sounds muddy.
lessons.pattern: C bar: C3-G3-G2-C4; G bar: G2-G3-D3-B3; quarters
quiz: Alternating bass places the fifth here on...

lessons.title: Original piece: River Thread
lessons.goal: Combine a picked melody with a measured bass line.
steps: Harmony C-G-Am-F, one bar each. RH thumb plays the root on1 and3; fingers play melody on2 and4.
Melody pairs are E4-G4, D4-G4, C4-E4, A3-C4; find the notes before joining bass.
Play four bars twice, bringing the melody forward but keeping the thumb pulse even. Use the partial F shape if a full barre is not ready.
lessons.pattern: C-G-Am-F; bass on1,3, melody on2,4; original four-bar fingerstyle
quiz: To hear the melody clearly, aim for...
Balanced treble above a stable bass pulse
Bass louder than every treble note

lessons.title: An optional full F barre
lessons.goal: Test a full F shape without using painful pressure.
steps: The full F shape is 133211 low-to-high. Place the index near fret1 and add fingers for frets2 and3.
Check individual strings with only enough pressure to sound; try slightly rolling the index to its firmer side while keeping a neutral wrist.
Practise one chord then rest. Use the existing partial F xx3211 if the full shape causes pain or strain; a teacher can adjust setup and technique.
lessons.pattern: F barre 133211; partial F xx3211 remains a valid alternative
quiz: If barre practice hurts you should...
Stop, rest and use a smaller shape or seek setup advice

lessons.title: A-root B minor shape
lessons.goal: Connect Bm, G, D and A with clear chord quality.
steps: Bm is x24432: root B2 on string5 fret2; third D4 on string2 fret3.
Check each string and compare B-D minor third with A-C# major third in A x02220.
Play Bm-G-D-A four beats per chord; if Bm is not clear yet, play its B-D-F# tones separately and mark weak chord for review.

lessons.title: Find octaves, not random frets
lessons.goal: Locate octave-related notes across the neck.
steps: A2 on string6 fret5 pairs with A3 string4 fret7; G2 fret3 pairs with G3 string4 fret5.
For a root on string5, its octave lies two strings thinner and two frets higher on string3.
Compare first-string fret12 E5 with open E4; the twelfth fret doubles frequency. Write three octave pairs and test by ear.
quiz: The same string at fret12 is...

lessons.title: One-octave A major in position
lessons.goal: Play A major with C#, F# and G#.
steps: Use string6 frets5,7,9 for A2,B2,C#3; string5 frets5,7,9 for D3,E3,F#3; string4 frets6,7 for G#3,A3.
Shift the hand for fret9 instead of forcing a four-fret stretch; rehearse shifts without sound first.
Compare to A natural minor by naming C#-F#-G#. Keep the pulse through both string and position changes.
lessons.pattern: E:5,7,9; A:5,7,9; D:6,7; A-major octave

lessons.title: Original piece: Highway Shapes
lessons.goal: Perform a movable-chord accompaniment with a stable groove.
steps: Use Bm-G-D-A for eight bars, two bars per chord, with attacks on1,2&,4.
First play root notes alone to learn the form, then add full or reduced chord voicings.
Give two takes at the ladder target with deliberate string muting. If a chord still buzzes, lower tempo and return to its string-by-string drill.
lessons.pattern: 8 bars: Bm Bm G G D D A A; strums1,2&,4
quiz: Two bars on each of four chords gives...

lessons.title: An alternating-thumb framework
lessons.goal: Keep thumb quarters under treble offbeats.
steps: On C alternate thumb C3 on1, G2 on2, C3 on3, G2 on4.
Add index G3 on1& and3&, middle C4 on2& and4&; isolate two beats before a full bar.
Maintain thumb time even when the treble finger misses. This is one original alternating-thumb pattern, not a copy of a song.
lessons.pattern: C: thumb C3-G2-C3-G2 on beats; treble G3-C4-G3-C4 on &

lessons.title: Controlled hammer-on and pull-off
lessons.goal: Make a short slur without an extra picking attack.
steps: On string2 pick fret1 C4, then place finger3 at fret3 D4 with a compact hammer-on.
Reverse by picking D and gently releasing finger3 so held fret1 C sounds; avoid pulling the string far sideways.
Compare picked C-D-C with slurred C-D-C at equal durations. Stop if fingertip or wrist pain appears.
lessons.pattern: B string1h3p1; three equal notes; one initial pick
quiz: A fretting-finger attack after the initial pick

lessons.title: Read a tuning change safely
lessons.goal: Adapt only the sixth-string map for drop D.
steps: Standard string6 E2 can be lowered one whole tone to D2; tune by ear/reference and return to standard after this exercise.
The other five strings remain unchanged. Low-string fret2 is now E2, fret3 F2 and fret5 G2.
Write a low-string riff D-E-F-G, play it on your instrument, and note that the app's fretboard still assumes standard tuning; use its pitch references rather than its low-string locations.
lessons.pattern: Drop-D real instrument string6:0,2,3,5; app diagram remains standard EADGBE
quiz: In drop D, which standard string changes?
Only string6, E2 down to D2
All strings up a whole tone

lessons.title: A capo changes sounding key
lessons.goal: Distinguish a chord shape from its sounding key.
steps: Without capo, C-F-G shapes sound C-F-G. With capo2, the same shapes sound D-G-A.
Play a short C-shape pattern with and without capo2, naming actual sounding notes.
Use the tuner to verify sounding D while fretting a C shape relative to capo2. The diagrams use absolute standard frets; count capo-relative frets yourself.
lessons.pattern: Capo2: C/F/G shapes sound D/G/A; app targets sounding notes

lessons.title: Original piece: Woven Lines
lessons.goal: Combine thumb pulse, treble melody and a slurred decoration.
steps: Use C-Am-F-G four bars. Thumb plays root/fifth alternation on numbered beats.
Melody starts E4-G4, then E4-C4, then A3-C4, then B3-D4; add a C4-D4-C4 hammer/pull in the second cycle only.
Write the decoration as subdivisions inside one beat rather than extra time. Perform a plain take and a decorated take with the same bass pulse.
lessons.pattern: C-Am-F-G; alternating bass quarters; treble offbeats, optional B:1h3p1 decoration

lessons.title: Seventh-chord colours
lessons.goal: Hear Cmaj7, Dm7 and G7 as different chord qualities.
steps: Use Cmaj7 x32000, Dm7 xx0211 and G7 320001; pick sounded strings before strumming.
Name Cmaj7 C-E-G-B, Dm7 D-F-A-C and G7 G-B-D-F.
Compare each shape with a triad. Listen for the seventh rather than assuming any four-note chord is dominant.

lessons.title: ii-V-I without extra motion
lessons.goal: Connect Dm7-G7-Cmaj7 with a clear cadence.
steps: Practise each shape separately, then Dm7 to G7 and G7 to Cmaj7 as slow pairs.
Use four beats per chord followed by a second Cmaj7 bar; bass notes D-G-C make the cadence audible.
Focus on F resolving to E and B remaining or resolving to C. Small comfortable voicings are preferable to a painful full-neck grip.
lessons.pattern: | Dm7 | G7 | Cmaj7 | Cmaj7 |; follow F->E and B->C
quiz: The ii chord in C major is...

lessons.title: D Dorian from C-major notes
lessons.goal: Play a D-Dorian octave and hear its natural sixth.
steps: Use D3 string4 open, E3 fret2, F3 fret3; G3 string3 open, A3 fret2, B3 fret4; C4 string2 fret1, D4 fret3.
Compare B natural to Bb in D natural minor.
Over Dm7 land on D,F,A,C and use B as a colour. Sing the phrase before placing it on the neck.

lessons.title: Read a sparse comping rhythm
lessons.goal: Place two chord attacks without filling every subdivision.
steps: Write a bar with attacks on beat1 and the & after3; both chords ring until the next attack or marked rest.
Apply to Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7 with continuous quiet strumming-hand motion.
Sing a melody while comping. Remove pedal-like excessive ringing by releasing pressure lightly, and keep space around the line.
lessons.pattern: Each 4/4 bar: chord on1 and3&; sparse ii-V-I comp

lessons.title: Original piece: Cafe Steps
lessons.goal: Play a ii-V-I melody then accompany its answer.
steps: Play melody alone first; on a second take comp the chord sequence and sing the melody.
Create one two-beat melodic variation ending on a chord tone. Compare the original and variation while preserving all four bars.
lessons.pattern: Dm7-G7-Cmaj7-Cmaj7; original half/quarter-note melody
quiz: The final two harmony bars are...

lessons.title: Optional bends with a target
lessons.goal: Check a modest bend against a known target pitch.
steps: On string2 fret3 D4, first play fret4 Eb4 as a reference, then return to D and try a gentle semitone bend.
Support the bending finger with nearby fingers and rotate the hand modestly; avoid wrenching the fingertip or pushing through pain.
Use the tuner to approach Eb, release back to D cleanly, and compare with a slide if your acoustic strings are too stiff. Never force a whole-tone bend.
lessons.pattern: B:3 -> semitone bend to Eb -> D; slide3-4-3 is a safe alternative
quiz: A controlled bend should be judged against...
A target pitch and comfortable motion

lessons.title: Major and minor pentatonic choices
lessons.goal: Compare A-major and A-minor pentatonic thirds.
steps: A major pentatonic is A-B-C#-E-F#; A minor is A-C-D-E-G.
Locate both slowly in a comfortable position and sing C# versus C over an A-major root chord.
Make a short major-colour answer and a minor-colour call. Land deliberately on A or E; do not randomly mix all chromatic notes.
lessons.pattern: A B C# E F#; A C D E G; major-colour answer to minor-colour call

lessons.title: Write space into a solo
lessons.goal: Develop a motif without abandoning the pulse.
steps: Write A-C-D-E as four eighths on beats1-2, then rest beats3-4.
Repeat the motif, change only its last note, then move its starting beat to2 while retaining four beats total.
Count aloud through every rest and limit the solo to four bars. Record weak rhythm when the shifted entrance drifts.
lessons.pattern: A C D E on1&2&; rest3-4; repeat with varied ending
quiz: A two-beat phrase followed by two beats rest fills...

lessons.title: A-B-A arrangement roadmap
lessons.goal: Plan a twelve-bar arrangement with contrast and return.
steps: Define A as four bars Am-F-C-G and B as four bars Dm-Am-E7-Am; write A-B-A.
Choose fingerpicking for first A, strums for B, and a lead motif above roots for final A.
Number twelve bars and name the E7 return to Am. Rehearse section boundaries separately before the complete performance.
lessons.pattern: 12-bar A-B-A: A Am-F-C-G; B Dm-Am-E7-Am; A returns
quiz: The E7 third leading into Am is...

lessons.title: Original piece: Homeward
lessons.goal: Perform an A-B-A acoustic arrangement with a personal variation.
steps: A melody | A C E C | A C F E | G E D C | B D G(2) |; B melody | D F A F | E C A(2) | G# B E B | A(4) |.
Use the previous twelve-bar chord roadmap, one bar per chord. Learn the melody apart from accompaniment and choose simple roots if simultaneous fingerstyle is not controlled.
Give two complete takes: picked A, strummed or sung B, varied final A. Assess chord clarity, pulse, phrase shape and written form, not just pitch hits.
lessons.pattern: Original 12-bar A-B-A over Am-F-C-G / Dm-Am-E7-Am / Am-F-C-G
quiz: The planned form and intentional rhythm
Every possible note at maximum speed
